newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate shoots up to 12 vs 10.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate shoots up to 12 vs 10.9 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate shot up to 12 percent on Wednesday from 10.9 percent after most bank lenders raised their prices.
Almost all of the 36.5 million kuna demand was met, leaving a slight surplus in the money market trade.
Most term interbank rates rose by one percentage point to between 13 and 17 percent, but call money was steady at 11 percent.
Insurers rolled over one-week loans at an unchanged nine percent, with a rate for 30-day funds at 13 percent.
The kuna midrates for Thursday firmed slightly at 6.0121 against the dollar and eased against the German mark. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
